findings.issue_text: [BUG] The OR branch in scheduleSMSReminders.ts:33-42 deleting reminders with retryCount > 1 is not constrained to method: SMS, so EMAIL reminders and SMS reminders with future scheduledDate are also deleted; the delete also fires at top of handler before fetch, deleting a reminder whose retry succeeded earlier in the same run

[BUG] The retry increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write on in-memory reminder.retryCount instead of prisma's { increment: 1 }, so overlapping cron invocations both read retryCount 0 and write 1, never tripping the retry cap and retrying indefinitely with duplicate SMS and Twilio cost

[ADVISORY] Cap enforcement lives only in the next run's deleteMany rather than co-located with the fetch or send decision, so nothing skips reminders already over the cap and cleanup/reordering of the deleteMany would silently remove the cap

[ADVISORY] New retryCount column is method-agnostic in schema and query but semantically SMS-only, so a future feature reusing the column for another reminder method gets cross-method deletion; the deleteMany query should be method-scoped now

[BUG] The new OR branch in the deleteMany at packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:28-42 deletes workflow reminders matching retryCount > 1 with no method filter and no scheduledDate filter — the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS constraint exists only inside the first OR arm, so reminders of any method (EMAIL, etc.) that hit retryCount 2 are permanently destroyed on the next cron run regardless of scheduled state, causing silent data loss.

[BUG] The retry cap is enforced as retryCount > 1, allowing exactly one retry before hard-deleting the reminder. Two transient Twilio/API failures on consecutive cron runs permanently drop the reminder — likely not the intended retry policy, and the diff states no intended cap.

[ADVISORY] No tests exist for the new non-trivial behavior (retry increments in the else branch and catch, the new deleteMany OR clause, the expanded select), so regressions like the missing method filter or retry-count arithmetic errors would ship undetected.

[ADVISORY] The catch block at scheduleSMSReminders.ts:186-194 unconditionally increments retryCount even for non-retryable errors (invalid phone number, suspended Twilio account, malformed payload), eventually deleting the reminder with only a console.log diagnostic — permanent failures silently vanish instead of surfacing an alertable error.

[ADVISORY] The else branch at scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178-183 increments retryCount when SMS scheduling returns without a sid, but there's no acceptance criterion for what 'scheduled but sid missing' means — if the SMS provider SDK changes response shape so sid is undefined while SMS is actually queued, every successfully-sent reminder is double-counted and deleted, causing duplicate sends followed by record loss.

[ADVISORY] Concurrent cron runs (overlapping invocations or multiple instances) can both findMany the same unscheduled reminder, both call the SMS provider, and both update retryCount — causing duplicate SMS sends and a retryCount race that can prematurely push a reminder over the deletion threshold; the new retryCount arithmetic makes this pre-existing duplication risk newly destructive.

[BUG] The new OR branch in scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31-41 deletes on retryCount > 1 without the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so the cleanup sweep deletes WorkflowReminder rows of any method whose retryCount exceeds 1, hard-deleting non-SMS reminders and cancelling reminders outside SMS scope; the method filter must be on both branches of the OR

[BUG] The catch block in scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178-186/189-196 increments retryCount unconditionally for every error type, including permanent non-retryable failures (invalid booking.phone, missing workflow step, malformed payload), causing reminders with permanently invalid phone numbers to be retried until retryCount > 1 purges them; retry logic has no distinction between transient and permanent failures

[ADVISORY] The retry cap is enforced only indirectly via a silent hard-delete in the cleanup query while the fetch selecting reminders to schedule does not filter on retryCount, making the max-2-attempts invariant implicit, untested, and coupled to deletion ordering

[ADVISORY] Zero tests cover the new behavior-bearing paths (increment on scheduling-failure, increment in catch, purge at retryCount > 1), risking silent deletion or infinite retries of customer reminders in EE paid SMS functionality

[ADVISORY] retryCount is added to the shared WorkflowReminder model but only written by the SMS endpoint, advertising an invariant no non-SMS writer enforces and inviting cross-method deletion; scoping the column or its consumers to SMS would have prevented the drift

[BUG] The prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch in scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178-193 is itself unguarded; if it throws (e.g. P2025 from a concurrent deleteMany or transient DB failure), the exception escapes the catch, aborts the for-loop, leaves every remaining reminder in the batch unscheduled, and returns a 500 instead of { ok: true }, turning per-reminder failures into batch-poisoning failures.

[ADVISORY] The new OR: [{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] delete branch in scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31-41 has no method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter and no scheduledDate bound, so if any other reminder channel (e.g. email) adopts the retryCount field on the shared WorkflowReminder model, this deleteMany silently hard-deletes the other channel's failed reminders.

[ADVISORY] Retry terminal state is represented by hard-deleting the row (retryCount > 1 → deleteMany) rather than a terminal status/flag column, losing all audit trail that a reminder was attempted and permanently failed; also the retry semantics use a magic number (gt: 1) with increments in two sites and no named constant, so a mismatch silently changes the retry count.

[ADVISORY] The retry mechanism widens the pre-existing fetch-then-act race in scheduleSMSReminders.ts:44-60: overlapping invocations both fetch the same unscheduled reminder with no atomic claim or conditional updateMany guard on the increment (read-modify-write on stale in-memory retryCount), causing double-sends and lost updates on retryCount; an atomic updateMany with a row-count check would close both windows.

[BUG] The deleteMany hard-deletes WorkflowReminder rows matching retryCount > 1 with no method filter, expanding the destructive delete beyond the SMS scope; the shared WorkflowReminder table means other reminder methods' rows can be silently and irreversibly deleted by the SMS cron

[ADVISORY] Objective drift: after two failed attempts the reminder is deleted with no persisted failure state, operator-visible flag, or audit trail beyond a console.log, making it impossible to distinguish 'never scheduled' from 'delivery permanently failed'

[ADVISORY] The retry cap is an unreviewed magic number embedded in the delete query (gt: 1) rather than a named, configurable limit, so tuning retry behavior requires reverse-engineering the cap from a Prisma filter and touching the destructive delete query

[ADVISORY] The two new retryCount increment blocks are copy-pasted identical prisma.workflowReminder.update calls, and neither the increments, the deleteMany OR branch, nor the migration default is covered by any test in the diff

[ADVISORY] The catch path increments retryCount uniformly for every error class, so transient Twilio 500s and permanent 400s (invalid phone number) both consume the same retry budget before permanent silent deletion, collapsing error semantics into one counter

[BUG] The new OR branch drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so any WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1 is deleted regardless of method, permanently deleting EMAIL and other method reminders that share the retryCount field

[BUG] The retry mechanism defeats itself: after two failures the reminder row is deleted by the cleanup that was supposed to reschedule it, and since the delete runs before the fetch, failed SMS reminders with retryCount > 1 are silently dropped rather than retried

[BUG] Reminders that failed while their scheduledDate is still in the future are deleted mid-retry, losing the reminder for the attendee (data loss of reminder records caused by transient Twilio errors pushing retryCount past 1)
[ADVISORY] The catch block logs the raw error object, which may include Twilio request details, account SID/auth material, and recipient phone numbers — PII/credential material written to log output

[ADVISORY] The workflowReminder.update calls in the else branch and catch block run without error handling; if the update throws, the exception propagates out of the loop, aborts scheduling of remaining reminders, and loses the original Twilio error

[BUG] The `OR: { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` branch of the `deleteMany` in scheduleSMSReminders.ts unconditionally destroys reminder rows that have exhausted two attempts, including ones that were successfully scheduled; the correct pattern is to skip scheduling on `retryCount > 1`, not delete the row

[BUG] `retryCount` is never reset on success, so the counter permanently marks any reminder that ever hit a transient failure, allowing the deleteMany to destroy reminders holding a valid `referenceId`

[ADVISORY] The `retryCount > 1` delete predicate has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` guard, unlike the sibling OR branch, so future writers incrementing `retryCount` on other channels could have reminders silently destroyed

[ADVISORY] The catch-path increment uses the stale in-memory `reminder.retryCount` instead of an atomic `increment: 1`, so concurrent invocations can both write the same value, inflating the retry budget and causing duplicate sends

[BUG] deleteMany uses an OR that deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method or scheduledDate, so an SMS reminder failing twice is hard-deleted while the endpoint returns { ok: true }, silently and permanently dropping the reminder with no error result, log entry, or recovery path

[BUG] The catch block increments retryCount and only console.logs, so a transient Twilio/auth/network failure becomes a silent retry counter bump; after the second bump the row is deleted, permanently cancelling the reminder with no notification or API error

[ADVISORY] The OR predicate drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS guard from the retryCount > 1 branch, so any reminder of another method (EMAIL or WHATSAPP) with retryCount > 1 would be mass-deleted by this SMS-only endpoint

[ADVISORY] retryCount is read in the initial findMany snapshot and incremented from that stale value with no transaction or atomic increment, so overlapping endpoint invocations both read 0, both write 1, and both send — causing duplicate SMS sends and retry budget undercounting, with no in-flight/lock guard on the unscheduled-reminder scan

goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The OR branch in scheduleSMSReminders.ts:33-42 deleting reminders with retryCount > 1 is not constrained to method: SMS, so EMAIL reminders and SMS reminders with future scheduledDate are also deleted; the delete also fires at top of handler before fetch, deleting a reminder whose retry succeeded earlier in the same run

[ADVISORY] Cap enforcement lives only in the next run's deleteMany rather than co-located with the fetch or send decision, so nothing skips reminders already over the cap and cleanup/reordering of the deleteMany would silently remove the cap

adjudication.rationale: The diff enforces the retry cap only via the initial `deleteMany` filter (`OR: [{method: SMS & scheduledDate <= now}, {retryCount: {gt: 1}}]`). The later fetch of `unscheduledReminders` does not filter on `retryCount`, and the send/update logic only increments `retryCount` (in both the `else` branch and `catch`) without any in-loop skip when over the cap. So the cap behavior is effectively coupled to that top-of-handler cleanup ordering; moving/removing/reordering that `deleteMany` would silently remove cap enforcement. This is a real, diff-grounded robustness/architecture concern, not necessarily a current functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New retryCount column is method-agnostic in schema and query but semantically SMS-only, so a future feature reusing the column for another reminder method gets cross-method deletion; the deleteMany query should be method-scoped now

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts, the cleanup `deleteMany` changed from being SMS-scoped to `OR: [{ method: SMS & scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`. The second branch is not constrained by `method`, so this endpoint can delete WorkflowReminder rows of other methods whenever their `retryCount > 1` (the new column is method-agnostic in schema.prisma). That is an unintended cross-method deletion risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new OR branch in the deleteMany at packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:28-42 deletes workflow reminders matching retryCount > 1 with no method filter and no scheduledDate filter — the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS constraint exists only inside the first OR arm, so reminders of any method (EMAIL, etc.) that hit retryCount 2 are permanently destroyed on the next cron run regardless of scheduled state, causing silent data loss.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the `deleteMany` filter was changed to `where: { OR: [ { method: SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: now } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] }`. The second OR arm (`retryCount > 1`) has no `method` or `scheduledDate` constraint, so it will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` record (including non-SMS methods and/or future scheduled dates) once its `retryCount` exceeds 1. Given the migration adds `retryCount` to the shared `WorkflowReminder` model, this can cause unintended permanent deletion/data loss beyond the intended “past SMS reminders” cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The retry cap is enforced as retryCount > 1, allowing exactly one retry before hard-deleting the reminder. Two transient Twilio/API failures on consecutive cron runs permanently drop the reminder — likely not the intended retry policy, and the diff states no intended cap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does enforce a hard cap by deleting any WorkflowReminder with `retryCount > 1` at the start of the handler (`deleteMany` OR clause). Since `retryCount` starts at 0 and is incremented on scheduling failure (both the `else` branch and `catch`), two failures will make `retryCount` reach 2, and the next cron run will delete the reminder before retrying again. That behavior is real and could be undesirable, but the diff doesn’t state the intended retry policy, so calling it a definite bug relies on assumptions about intent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No tests exist for the new non-trivial behavior (retry increments in the else branch and catch, the new deleteMany OR clause, the expanded select), so regressions like the missing method filter or retry-count arithmetic errors would ship undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds non-trivial new behavior (deleteMany now uses an OR that can delete records based solely on retryCount > 1; the query select now includes retryCount; and retryCount is incremented in both the `else` branch and the `catch`). This PR does not add or modify any tests alongside those changes, so the advisory about missing test coverage for these new code paths is a specific, diff-grounded review concern (even if we cannot prove no tests exist elsewhere in the repo).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The catch block at scheduleSMSReminders.ts:186-194 unconditionally increments retryCount even for non-retryable errors (invalid phone number, suspended Twilio account, malformed payload), eventually deleting the reminder with only a console.log diagnostic — permanent failures silently vanish instead of surfacing an alertable error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `retryCount` and unconditionally increments it in both the `else` branch and the `catch` block (`prisma.workflowReminder.update(... retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1)`) without checking error type. It also changes cleanup to delete reminders where `retryCount > 1` via an `OR` condition in `deleteMany`, meaning repeated failures will cause reminders to be removed with only a `console.log` as diagnostics. This behavior (eventual silent deletion after generic failures) is directly introduced by the diff and can lead to dropped reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The else branch at scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178-183 increments retryCount when SMS scheduling returns without a sid, but there's no acceptance criterion for what 'scheduled but sid missing' means — if the SMS provider SDK changes response shape so sid is undefined while SMS is actually queued, every successfully-sent reminder is double-counted and deleted, causing duplicate sends followed by record loss.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds logic where, after attempting to schedule an SMS, the code treats a falsy/missing `scheduledSMS.sid` as failure and increments `retryCount` (new else branch), and also increments `retryCount` in the catch. Separately, the cleanup at the start now deletes any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1` (regardless of method/date). This makes the system sensitive to the assumption that a successful provider response always includes `sid`; if that assumption is ever wrong, the reminder can be retried (duplicate sends) and then deleted once `retryCount` exceeds 1. The diff doesn’t prove the provider can succeed without `sid`, so it’s a robustness/spec/acceptance-criteria concern rather than a verified defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Concurrent cron runs (overlapping invocations or multiple instances) can both findMany the same unscheduled reminder, both call the SMS provider, and both update retryCount — causing duplicate SMS sends and a retryCount race that can prematurely push a reminder over the deletion threshold; the new retryCount arithmetic makes this pre-existing duplication risk newly destructive.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces retryCount-based behavior that is vulnerable to concurrent runs: reminders are selected via `findMany` with no locking/claiming, so overlapping invocations can process the same `reminder` and both attempt to schedule SMS. Additionally, the retry counter is updated as `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` (in both the `else` branch and `catch`), which is a non-atomic read-modify-write and can race under concurrency. With the new deletion condition `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`, races/double-processing can prematurely push a reminder over the deletion threshold, causing loss of future scheduling attempts and potentially duplicate sends.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new OR branch in scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31-41 deletes on retryCount > 1 without the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so the cleanup sweep deletes WorkflowReminder rows of any method whose retryCount exceeds 1, hard-deleting non-SMS reminders and cancelling reminders outside SMS scope; the method filter must be on both branches of the OR

[BUG] The catch block in scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178-186/189-196 increments retryCount unconditionally for every error type, including permanent non-retryable failures (invalid booking.phone, missing workflow step, malformed payload), causing reminders with permanently invalid phone numbers to be retried until retryCount > 1 purges them; retry logic has no distinction between transient and permanent failures

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show retryCount being incremented in both the new `else` branch and the `catch` block (new `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } })`), with no branching on error type. It also deletes reminders where `retryCount > 1` via `deleteMany`’s new `OR` condition. However, from the diff alone it’s not verifiable that this is a correctness “bug” vs. an intentional coarse retry policy (retry a couple times, then purge). The finding’s request to distinguish transient vs permanent errors is a reasonable review concern created by the change, but not a demonstrable defect solely from the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retry cap is enforced only indirectly via a silent hard-delete in the cleanup query while the fetch selecting reminders to schedule does not filter on retryCount, making the max-2-attempts invariant implicit, untested, and coupled to deletion ordering

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the only explicit “cap” behavior is the initial cleanup `deleteMany` with an `OR` clause that hard-deletes records where `retryCount > 1`. The subsequent `findMany` that selects reminders to schedule does not filter on `retryCount` (it only adds `retryCount: true` to `select`), so the max-attempts rule is enforced only because deletion happens before fetching in this handler. That makes the invariant implicit and coupled to this ordering, rather than being expressed in the scheduling query/logic itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Zero tests cover the new behavior-bearing paths (increment on scheduling-failure, increment in catch, purge at retryCount > 1), risking silent deletion or infinite retries of customer reminders in EE paid SMS functionality

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior-bearing logic around `retryCount` (purging reminders with `retryCount > 1` via `deleteMany` OR-clause, selecting `retryCount`, and incrementing it both on a non-`scheduledSMS` path and in `catch`). No corresponding test additions/updates are shown in this PR diff to validate these new branches and their interaction with deletion criteria, so requesting tests for these specific paths is a concrete review concern. However, the claim that *zero* tests cover it cannot be strictly verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] retryCount is added to the shared WorkflowReminder model but only written by the SMS endpoint, advertising an invariant no non-SMS writer enforces and inviting cross-method deletion; scoping the column or its consumers to SMS would have prevented the drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `retryCount` to the shared `WorkflowReminder` model (Prisma schema + migration) but only the SMS scheduling endpoint reads/writes it (`select: { ...select, retryCount: true }` and `update` increments). Also, the cleanup query in this SMS endpoint deletes reminders with `retryCount > 1` without scoping to `method: SMS` (`deleteMany` uses `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate... }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`), which couples a shared-field invariant to one endpoint and could affect non-SMS reminders if any other writer ever sets `retryCount`. This is a concrete scope/architecture concern grounded in the diff, though not necessarily an immediate defect if non-SMS reminders never get `retryCount > 1`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch in scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178-193 is itself unguarded; if it throws (e.g. P2025 from a concurrent deleteMany or transient DB failure), the exception escapes the catch, aborts the for-loop, leaves every remaining reminder in the batch unscheduled, and returns a 500 instead of { ok: true }, turning per-reminder failures into batch-poisoning failures.

adjudication.rationale: In the per-reminder try/catch, the `catch (error)` block now calls `await prisma.workflowReminder.update({ where: { id: reminder.id }, data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } })` with no additional guarding. If that update throws (e.g., record was deleted by the earlier `deleteMany` OR clause / concurrent process, causing Prisma P2025, or a transient DB failure), the exception will escape the `catch`, abort the loop, and fail the whole request rather than isolating the failure to that reminder. This is a real batch-poisoning failure mode introduced/exposed by the added update call in the catch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new OR: [{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] delete branch in scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31-41 has no method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter and no scheduledDate bound, so if any other reminder channel (e.g. email) adopts the retryCount field on the shared WorkflowReminder model, this deleteMany silently hard-deletes the other channel's failed reminders.

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts the prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany() `where` clause was changed to `OR: [...]` where the second branch is only `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` (no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and no `scheduledDate` bound). This will hard-delete *any* WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1 regardless of channel/method, contradicting the comment/intended scope (“delete all scheduled sms reminders...”) and creating real risk of deleting non-SMS reminders stored in the same table.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Retry terminal state is represented by hard-deleting the row (retryCount > 1 → deleteMany) rather than a terminal status/flag column, losing all audit trail that a reminder was attempted and permanently failed; also the retry semantics use a magic number (gt: 1) with increments in two sites and no named constant, so a mismatch silently changes the retry count.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does implement a terminal retry state by permanently deleting records via `deleteMany({ where: { OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] } })`, which removes any history/auditability of reminders that exceeded retries. The retry limit is also encoded as a magic number (`gt: 1`) while `retryCount` is incremented in two separate places (`else` branch and `catch`), with no shared constant, so future changes could silently desynchronize semantics. This is a concrete design/maintainability concern grounded in the shown code, but not a strictly verifiable correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retry mechanism widens the pre-existing fetch-then-act race in scheduleSMSReminders.ts:44-60: overlapping invocations both fetch the same unscheduled reminder with no atomic claim or conditional updateMany guard on the increment (read-modify-write on stale in-memory retryCount), causing double-sends and lost updates on retryCount; an atomic updateMany with a row-count check would close both windows.

adjudication.rationale: The diff continues a fetch-then-act pattern: reminders are loaded via `findMany` (now including `retryCount`) and later updated with `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` in separate `update` calls. There is no atomic “claim”/conditional `updateMany` guard tying scheduling + increment to current DB state, so overlapping invocations can act on the same reminder: both may attempt to schedule (double-send) and/or overwrite each other’s retryCount increment (lost update) because they use a stale in-memory `reminder.retryCount`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The deleteMany hard-deletes WorkflowReminder rows matching retryCount > 1 with no method filter, expanding the destructive delete beyond the SMS scope; the shared WorkflowReminder table means other reminder methods' rows can be silently and irreversibly deleted by the SMS cron

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts, the prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany() `where` clause was changed to `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`. The `retryCount > 1` branch has no `method: SMS` filter, so this SMS scheduling job will hard-delete any WorkflowReminder row (of any method) with retryCount > 1, which expands deletion beyond the SMS scope stated by the comment and file purpose.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Objective drift: after two failed attempts the reminder is deleted with no persisted failure state, operator-visible flag, or audit trail beyond a console.log, making it impossible to distinguish 'never scheduled' from 'delivery permanently failed'

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `retryCount` and increments it on scheduling failure (`update` in the `else` branch and in `catch`), and then deletes reminders with `retryCount > 1` via `deleteMany({ where: { OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] } })`. This means after two failed attempts the record will be removed on a subsequent run, and there is no persisted terminal failure status/error/audit record kept (only a transient `console.log`), so operators can’t later distinguish “never scheduled” from “gave up after retries.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retry cap is an unreviewed magic number embedded in the delete query (gt: 1) rather than a named, configurable limit, so tuning retry behavior requires reverse-engineering the cap from a Prisma filter and touching the destructive delete query

adjudication.rationale: The diff hard-codes the retry limit as `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` inside the `deleteMany` OR filter. This embeds an implicit retry cap (2 attempts max before deletion) directly in a destructive query without a named constant/config, making the behavior non-obvious and harder to tune or audit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The two new retryCount increment blocks are copy-pasted identical prisma.workflowReminder.update calls, and neither the increments, the deleteMany OR branch, nor the migration default is covered by any test in the diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two identical `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ where: { id: reminder.id }, data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } })` blocks: one in the new `else` branch after attempting to schedule (`} else { ... }`) and one in the `catch` block, which is indeed copy-pasted duplication. Also, the diff introduces new nontrivial logic (the `deleteMany` `OR` branch including `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`, the `retryCount` selection/type change, and the migration default `DEFAULT 0`) but does not add or modify any test files in this diff, so there is no test coverage shown for these changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The catch path increments retryCount uniformly for every error class, so transient Twilio 500s and permanent 400s (invalid phone number) both consume the same retry budget before permanent silent deletion, collapsing error semantics into one counter

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a single retryCount that is incremented both when scheduling returns no SID (new `else` branch) and for any thrown error (new `catch`), with no differentiation by error type. It also deletes reminders with `retryCount > 1` via `deleteMany({ where: { OR: [...] }})`, effectively giving all failure modes the same retry budget and then removing the record. This is a real, diff-grounded design/behavior concern, but the diff alone doesn't prove it's incorrect vs intended, so it's not a definitive bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The retry mechanism defeats itself: after two failures the reminder row is deleted by the cleanup that was supposed to reschedule it, and since the delete runs before the fetch, failed SMS reminders with retryCount > 1 are silently dropped rather than retried

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly deletes any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1` via the new `deleteMany` `OR` clause, and this runs before the subsequent `findMany` fetch. So reminders that have failed twice (retryCount incremented on failure) will indeed be removed and won’t be retried on later runs. However, this looks like an intentional max-retry cap rather than a self-defeating bug, since nothing in the diff indicates the system is meant to retry indefinitely; the behavior is consistent with “drop after 2 failures.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Reminders that failed while their scheduledDate is still in the future are deleted mid-retry, losing the reminder for the attendee (data loss of reminder records caused by transient Twilio errors pushing retryCount past 1)

adjudication.rationale: The new cleanup query deletes any WorkflowReminder with `retryCount > 1` via an `OR` clause, regardless of `scheduledDate` or `method` (see `deleteMany({ where: { OR: [...] { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] } })`). Since the handler now increments `retryCount` on scheduling failure (both in the `else` branch and in `catch`), a reminder that fails twice (retryCount becomes 2) will be deleted at the start of the next run even if its `scheduledDate` is still in the future, causing loss of the reminder record.

While the specific claim that it will include Twilio account SID/auth material and recipient phone numbers isn’t verifiable from this diff alone, logging raw error objects from external API calls is a concrete, diff-grounded concern because such errors can include request/response details and thus risk leaking sensitive/PII into logs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The workflowReminder.update calls in the else branch and catch block run without error handling; if the update throws, the exception propagates out of the loop, aborts scheduling of remaining reminders, and loses the original Twilio error

adjudication.rationale: In the new logic, the catch block does `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` and then logs the Twilio error. If that Prisma update throws, it is not wrapped in a nested try/catch, so the exception will escape the loop and abort scheduling remaining reminders, and the original Twilio error won’t be logged because execution stops before `console.log`. (The else-branch update is inside the outer try/catch, but the catch-block update itself is unhandled.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The `OR: { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` branch of the `deleteMany` in scheduleSMSReminders.ts unconditionally destroys reminder rows that have exhausted two attempts, including ones that were successfully scheduled; the correct pattern is to skip scheduling on `retryCount > 1`, not delete the row

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `deleteMany` to `where: { OR: [ { method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] }`, which will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` row with `retryCount > 1` regardless of method, scheduledDate, or whether it was successfully scheduled (e.g., a reminder could have `retryCount` incremented on earlier failures, later succeed without resetting `retryCount`, and then be deleted on the next run). This is unconditional row destruction driven solely by retryCount.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `retryCount` is never reset on success, so the counter permanently marks any reminder that ever hit a transient failure, allowing the deleteMany to destroy reminders holding a valid `referenceId`

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces deletion of any WorkflowReminder with `retryCount > 1` via `deleteMany({ where: { OR: [...] , { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] } })` without restricting to unscheduled reminders or `referenceId` being null. The scheduling logic increments `retryCount` on failures (both in the `else` branch and in `catch`) but on success only updates `referenceId` and does not reset `retryCount`. Therefore a reminder that fails twice and later succeeds will retain `retryCount = 2` and can be deleted on the next run despite having a valid `referenceId`. This is a verifiable data-loss/correctness bug grounded in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `retryCount > 1` delete predicate has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` guard, unlike the sibling OR branch, so future writers incrementing `retryCount` on other channels could have reminders silently destroyed

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the `deleteMany` now uses `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`. The second branch has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so any `WorkflowReminder` record (regardless of channel/method) with `retryCount > 1` would be deleted by this endpoint, creating a real risk of unintended data loss as soon as non-SMS reminders ever have `retryCount` incremented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The catch-path increment uses the stale in-memory `reminder.retryCount` instead of an atomic `increment: 1`, so concurrent invocations can both write the same value, inflating the retry budget and causing duplicate sends

adjudication.rationale: In both the `else` branch and the `catch` block, the PR updates `retryCount` via `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` (using the value read earlier in `unscheduledReminders`). This is a non-atomic read-modify-write; concurrent invocations handling the same reminder can overwrite each other and fail to reliably increment `retryCount`. Since cleanup/deletion is based on `retryCount > 1`, missed increments can effectively extend the allowed retries and contribute to repeated scheduling attempts/duplicate sends. Using Prisma's atomic `increment: 1` would avoid this race.

The second OR branch has no `method`/date constraint, so it will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1`, including non-SMS reminders and reminders not past due. Since `retryCount` is incremented on failure in this handler, a reminder that fails twice will be hard-deleted on the next run with no explicit error path in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The catch block increments retryCount and only console.logs, so a transient Twilio/auth/network failure becomes a silent retry counter bump; after the second bump the row is deleted, permanently cancelling the reminder with no notification or API error
